Subject: Correction to the daily takings GST template: please check before filing

Draft only — not for publication yet.

There is an error in the GST formula in versions v1.0, v1.1 and v1.2 of my daily takings template. If you used one of these versions to record GST-inclusive takings, please stop using it and check your figures before filing. The corrected version, v1.3, was uploaded on 8 Nov and is available from the download link on the original post.

The template has been downloaded 412 times since 12 Aug. Not everyone who downloaded it will be affected, but this needs a proper correction, not just a change to the file.

What went wrong

Column F multiplied the takings entered by 9%. That is correct when the amount entered excludes GST. It is not correct when the amount already includes GST.

For GST-inclusive takings, the GST portion is 9/109 of the amount, not 9%.

Ravi’s example makes the difference clear. His GST-inclusive takings were $1,090. The old formula calculated $98.10 in GST. The correct GST is $90, a difference of $8.10.

The error affects people who entered GST-inclusive takings, which will include most hawkers using the sheet. Entries that excluded GST were not affected. In the quarterly summary, the error affected Box 6, the output tax figure. The Box 1 sales total was calculated independently and was correct in these versions.

How I missed it

I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures, which were already exclusive of GST. The check passed. I did not properly test the inclusive-takings calculation before putting the template up.

That was my mistake. Melvin is right to be upset. People trusted the sheet because I am an accountant, and they should not now have to spend time checking and correcting work because of my formula. I am sorry for that.

Thank you to Ravi and Shu Fen for catching it and explaining the problem clearly.

What to do now

If you have not filed, download v1.3, transfer your takings and check the recalculated quarterly figures before using them in your return.

Please pay particular attention to H2. It must match the amounts you enter, not simply how you describe your menu prices. Select “prices exclude GST” only if the entries exclude GST. If you enter receipts that include GST collected, use the inclusive setting, even if your menu prices exclude GST.

If you already filed Q3 using the sheet:

1. Keep a copy of the original workbook and the return you submitted. Do not overwrite them. You will need a record of what was filed.

2. Check which version you used and whether the takings entered included GST. The affected versions are v1.0, v1.1 and v1.2.

3. If affected, transfer the same Q3 takings into v1.3 and set H2 correctly. Check the entries against your records so you are comparing the same transactions.

4. Compare the corrected quarterly Box 6 figure with your submitted return and record the difference. This formula error did not affect Box 1; do not reduce that figure just because Box 6 changes.

5. Before submitting a correction, read IRAS’s “Correcting Errors Made in GST Return” page and check with your filer, or IRAS if you file yourself. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error can be adjusted in a later GST F5 or requires a GST F7. Please do not simply deduct the difference from your next return without checking the correct route.

This particular error overstates GST. It did not cause anyone to underpay IRAS, but affected users may have overpaid. That still needs sorting out.

If you passed the old template to another stall owner, please pass this correction to them too.
